catalog_quote: In many cases, stress is insensitive to weight; in some languages, stress location is sensitive to morphosyntactic factors. One [Torricelli; Sandaun, PNG] regularly assigns stress to the penultimate syllable, but verbs allow for stress on either syllable of the final foot, resulting in contrasts such as [ˈte.re] ‘chop’ and [te.ˈre] ‘howl’. While forms like the noun [ˈte.li] ‘round thing’ would be equally legitimate for a verb, *[te.ˈli] with final stress is not a possible noun.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress is on the penultimate syllable (a right-aligned trochee). In verbs the position within the final disyllabic foot is lexically specified, so verbs contrast penultimate vs final stress ([ˈtere] 'chop' vs [teˈre] 'howl'); nouns (and by implication other non-verbs) never have final stress. Stress is not weight-sensitive.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: stress may fall on either syllable of the final foot, lexically (minimal pair [ˈte.re] 'chop' vs [te.ˈre] 'howl'); final stress is impossible in nouns (*[te.ˈli]). No other exceptions, clitic or affix effects discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement given in a typological survey paragraph with isolated citation forms; no discussion of phrase-level prosody for One. The chapter says only 'One [Torricelli; Sandaun, PNG]' without naming the variety; co-author Donohue's One fieldwork is on the Molmo village variety (Donohue 2000 fn. 1), and no other source is cited, so the data are evidently his own Molmo One field data.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source names the language only as 'One [Torricelli; Sandaun, PNG]'. Co-author Mark Donohue's One fieldwork (with Melissa Crowther, 1998-2001) was in Molmo village and he states elsewhere (Donohue 2000, fn. 1) that his label 'One' refers specifically to the Molmo variety, so the statement is taken to describe Molmo One (molm1235, ISO aun). Glottolog/ISO split One into six languages (Molmo, Inebu, Kabore, Kwamtim, Northern, Southern One); the statement should not be extended to the others without their own sources (e.g. Pehrson et al. 2016 for Northern One/Onnele, nort2907).
